messages.text: The S1 is/was Almost brand new and not overclocked. The initial power supply had issues with unsecured/intermittent contacts on the 240v supply side which I suspect may have something to do with the issue.

I'm Hal, HeliumDeploy's technical specialist, picking this up from Sarah.

Thanks, Laurie, that helps. Loose or intermittent contacts on the 240V side of a power supply can cause arcing and voltage spikes. Those can damage a miner's input stage. Since the fuse still blows with a new power supply, your theory fits what we're seeing.

Until this is sorted:

1. Please don't power the S1 again, and stop using the original power supply completely.

To build the full picture for the team, I need three things:

1. **Which fuse blows?** Is it the one in the wall plug, the one on the power supply, or one on the S1 itself?
2. **Did you ever notice sparking, a burning smell or a hot plug** with either power supply?
3. **A clear photo of the S1's serial number label.** Please also say which order it came on, if you know. I can see two orders from May on your account.

Please don't try to film it powering up, since that would just blow another fuse.
The BS2 was suppose to be a replacement for a Nerdoctax that you failed to deliver from my original order. It was suggested to me because it was in stock, and could be delivered immediately.
Passed the chat to support · BS-2 on Shop···· was a swap for an undelivered NerdOctaxe from the original o
I've handed your message back to Sarah because it's about the order rather than the hardware. Sarah will reply to it herself, so there's nothing more from me on this turn.

And in response to Hal. The fuse that blows is the 15amp automotive fuse that is on the S1 unit itself. 
The original power supply required setting

I'm Hal, HeliumDeploy's technical specialist, back on the S1.

Thanks, Laurie. Knowing it's the 15A blade fuse on the S1 itself helps a lot. A new power supply didn't stop that fuse blowing, so the fault is in the miner itself, after the fuse. The power supply isn't the problem.

Two safety points for now:

1. Don't fit any more fuses and try again.
2. Never fit a bigger fuse than the 15A. It's the only thing protecting the board.

Your last message got cut off at "The original power supply required setting". Could you finish that sentence? It sounds like the original supply needed fixing or adjusting, and that matters.

When you can, please also send:

1. A clear photo of the S1's serial number label.
2. The order the S1 came on, if you know it. Your account has two orders from May.

Thanks, Laurie. So the original power supply needed setting up by hand, and the loose contacts were on its 240V input. That fits your theory about what damaged the S1. I'll include it in my notes for the team.

Please don't use that original supply again, and don't try to fix its wiring. Mains connections need a qualified electrician.

To finish my findings, I need:

1. **A clear photo of the S1's serial number label.**
2. **Which May order the S1 came on**, if you know it.
(The customer sent this photo without a message.)

I opened your photo and recorded my findings on the S1 as a likely board fault. JD or Georges now decide whether to approve a return, and the chat has gone back to Sarah. I haven't sent the customer a message this turn, as the process says.

- **Photo:** it shows the label on the S1's board. Model Nexus S1-BTC, power input 12V XT30, serial (number hidden) as best I can read it.
- **Why a board fault:** the S1's own 15A fuse blows even with a new power supply. That points to a short inside the miner, not the power supply. Per JD's triage notes, that's a return-level fault for the S1.
- **Order not confirmed:** I can't see which May order the S1 came on, Shop···· or Shop····. I put both in the verdict, so someone needs to match the serial to the right order. The serial may contain a May 26 2026 date, which would be after both orders were placed. That's my guess from the number, not confirmed.
- **Customer's points I included:** they say it was almost new and never overclocked. The original power supply had to be set up by hand and had loose contacts on its 240V input. They think that caused the damage.
- **Not received:** no video. I didn't ask for one, because powering the unit blows the fuse again.

I told the customer to stop powering the S1, not to fit more or bigger fuses, and not to use or rewire the original power supply. Nobody has told them a return is approved.
